Asymptotic diversity estimates

Source: R/alpha.R
div_estimate.Rd

Estimates the asymptotic Hill numbers of order 0, 1 and 2 for each site using the Chao1 richness estimator, the Chao et al. (2013) Shannon estimator and the unbiased Simpson estimator. Standard errors and confidence intervals come from bootstrap resampling of the estimated community, as in iNEXT.

Usage

div_estimate(
  data,
  site = site,
  species = species,
  abundance = NULL,
  q = c(0, 1, 2),
  conf = 0.95,
  nboot = 50,
  ci = c("lognormal", "normal"),
  type = c("TD", "PD", "FD"),
  tree = NULL,
  reftime = NULL,
  pd_unit = c("mean", "total"),
  distance = NULL,
  tau = NULL,
  unit = NULL,
  n_units = NULL,
  .by = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame in long format, with one row per record.

site, species

<tidy-select> The column holding site identifiers and the column holding species names.

abundance

<tidy-select> The column holding counts. If NULL (the default), a column called abundance is used when present, otherwise every row counts as one individual.

q

Orders of diversity: any of 0, 1 and 2.

conf

Confidence level of the intervals.

nboot

Number of bootstrap replicates. Use 0 to skip them. For PD and FD the bootstrap community adds undetected species with estimated branch lengths (PD) or distances (FD); see Details in div_estimate().

ci

How to build the confidence intervals from the bootstrap standard error. With "lognormal" (the default) the richness (q = 0) interval uses the log-transformation of Chao (1987), as in SpadeR, so it is asymmetric and its lower limit never falls below the observed richness; orders 1 and 2 use estimate +/- z * se. With "normal" every order uses estimate +/- z * se, as in iNEXT::iNEXT(). In both cases the lower limit is truncated at the observed diversity, which the asymptotic diversity cannot fall below.

type

Diversity dimension: "TD" (taxonomic, the default), "PD" (phylogenetic, needs tree) or "FD" (functional, needs distance). Give several, such as c("TD", "PD"), or "all" for all three, to analyse the dimensions together: the results are stacked in one tibble with a type column, and autoplot() shows them side by side. All three are Hill numbers of the same order q, in units of effective numbers of species (Chao, Chiu and Jost 2014), and reproduce iNEXT.3D.

tree

For type = "PD", a rooted ape::phylo tree with branch lengths whose tip labels include every species.

reftime

For type = "PD", the reference time (tree depth) at which diversity is measured. Defaults to the age of the root of the tree pruned to the species in data.

pd_unit

For type = "PD", "mean" (the default) divides phylogenetic diversity by reftime, giving the effective number of lineages on the same scale as species; "total" gives effective total branch length.

distance

For type = "FD", a species-by-species distance matrix (or stats::dist object) with names matching the species, scaled to lie between 0 and 1, for example from Gower distances of traits.

tau

For type = "FD", the distance threshold below which species are treated as functionally identical. Defaults to the mean distance between two individuals in the pooled data. Use "auc" to integrate over all thresholds from 0 to 1 (Chao et al. 2019).

unit

For incidence data, the column naming the sampling unit (a trap, bait, plot or survey day) in which each species was detected. Each site is then described by the number of units in which each species was found and the number of units sampled, and every estimate is incidence-based (Chao et al. 2014), for TD, PD and FD alike. Leave NULL for abundance data.

n_units

For incidence data, a column giving the number of units sampled at each site, constant within a site. Use it when some units detected no species and so do not appear in the data. By default the number of distinct units in the data is used.

.by

<tidy-select> Optional grouping columns, kept in the output. Grouped data frames are also respected.

Value

A tibble with the grouping columns, the site column, q, observed, estimate, se, lower and upper.

Details

For type = "PD" and type = "FD" the bootstrap resamples an estimated community that includes undetected species, as for taxonomic diversity. Under PD each undetected species is given its own branch, of length equal to the estimated undetected branch length divided by the estimated number of undetected species (Chao et al. 2015; Hsieh and Chao 2017). Under FD undetected species are assumed to resemble the rarest observed species: their distance to each observed species is the mean distance from the singletons to that species, and their distance to each other is the mean distance among the singletons. The reference time (PD) and threshold tau (FD) are held fixed across replicates.

References

Chao, A., Gotelli, N. J., Hsieh, T. C., Sander, E. L., Ma, K. H., Colwell, R. K. and Ellison, A. M. (2014). Rarefaction and extrapolation with Hill numbers. Ecological Monographs, 84, 45-67. doi:10.1890/13-0133.1

Chao, A. (1987). Estimating the population size for capture-recapture data with unequal catchability. Biometrics, 43, 783-791. doi:10.2307/2531532

Examples

set.seed(1)
div_estimate(png_ants, .by = season, nboot = 20)
#> # A tibble: 30 × 8
#>    season site       q observed estimate    se lower upper
#>    <chr>  <chr>  <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#>  1 dry    MW0200     0    16       18.4   6.36 16.1   56.5
#>  2 dry    MW0200     1    12.3     15.2   1.34 12.6   17.8
#>  3 dry    MW0200     2     9.91    12.3   1.65  9.91  15.5
#>  4 dry    MW0700     0    15       83.9  40.6  38.6  216. 
#>  5 dry    MW0700     1    11.8     38.5  23.3  11.8   84.0
#>  6 dry    MW0700     2     8.67    13.3   9.48  8.67  31.9
#>  7 dry    MW1200     0    13       20.9  19.3  13.5  134. 
#>  8 dry    MW1200     1     9.37    13.8   4.82  9.37  23.3
#>  9 dry    MW1200     2     6.73     8.46  2.60  6.73  13.5
#> 10 dry    MW1700     0     5        5.24  1.51  5.01  15.4
#> # ℹ 20 more rows

# Incidence-based (Chao2) estimates, baits as sampling units
div_estimate(png_ants, unit = bait, n_units = baits, .by = season, nboot = 20)
#> # A tibble: 30 × 8
#>    season site       q observed estimate    se lower upper
#>    <chr>  <chr>  <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#>  1 dry    MW0200     0    16       18.5   6.44 16.1   57.1
#>  2 dry    MW0200     1    12.3     15.2   1.53 12.3   18.2
#>  3 dry    MW0200     2     9.91    12.3   1.43  9.91  15.1
#>  4 dry    MW0700     0    15       85.8  39.3  40.6  211. 
#>  5 dry    MW0700     1    11.8     39.2  20.1  11.8   78.7
#>  6 dry    MW0700     2     8.67    13.7   6.67  8.67  26.8
#>  7 dry    MW1200     0    13       21.0  11.3  14.0   75.2
#>  8 dry    MW1200     1     9.37    14.0   3.11  9.37  20.1
#>  9 dry    MW1200     2     6.73     8.61  2.19  6.73  12.9
#> 10 dry    MW1700     0     5        5.25  1.92  5.00  18.2
#> # ℹ 20 more rows
